name: A teacher gains a subject, and the menu follows
why: The switch the whole term turns on. Nobody edits a role: the school allocates a subject, and five screens appear on that person's next sign-in — which is how a head of department who starts teaching in January needs no role change at all.

steps.do: Look at a teacher who is allocated nothing, then allocate them one subject in one section.
steps.expect: Saved. This screen was read-only until today — it showed who taught what and gave no way to change it.

steps.do: Sign in as that teacher and open marks entry.
steps.expect: The paper dropdown offers that subject and nothing else in the school. Before the allocation the entry was not even in their menu.

steps.do: Take the allocation away again.
steps.expect: Marks entry, homework, lesson plans, the register and report cards leave that person's menu on their next refresh. Marks already entered are untouched.

name: Class teacher is a name on a section, not a role
why: A subject teacher marks their own subject; a class teacher collates the whole section. The difference is one field on the section, and it decides three different powers.

steps.do: Name a teacher as class teacher of one section.
steps.expect: Saved against the section — not against the person.

steps.do: As that teacher, generate report cards for the section.
steps.expect: Generated. A teacher who is not its class teacher is refused, naming why.

steps.do: Open student leave requests.
steps.expect: Their section's children are there to decide. Another section's are not.

name: Two roles a person may hold, and two they may not
why: A role is a workspace; a capability is a job. Two roles that draw the same screens are one workspace listed twice, and the person has to learn which copy to use.

steps.do: Give somebody the “Teacher & librarian” preset.
steps.expect: Both granted. Two icons on their left rail, nothing shared between them — and the librarian role installs itself if this school has never used it.

steps.do: Now try to give one person both HOD and Faculty.
steps.expect: Refused, and told what to do instead: allocate them a subject, and the hod role gives those screens by itself.

steps.do: Try Admissions together with Receptionist.
steps.expect: Refused. All five of the receptionist's entries are inside admissions, so it would be the front desk twice.

name: Attendance reaches the parent and the principal
why: One register mark is the school's whole absence story: the family is told, the principal's day-count moves, and the child's percentage changes.

steps.do: Mark one child absent in your own section, and save.
steps.expect: The register saves and says how many were marked.

steps.do: Open the child's attendance.
steps.expect: “<child> was marked absent”, and the percentage has dropped.

steps.do: Look at today's attendance figure.
steps.expect: The absent count includes that child — e.g. “1 absent · 90% · 9/10”.

name: Homework reaches the student and the parent
why: Set once by the teacher, read in two different apps — and the notification has to quote enough of it to be worth opening.

steps.do: Publish a piece of homework to one section, with a due date.
steps.expect: It appears in your own list as published.

steps.do: Open homework.
steps.expect: The same title and due date, and a notification quoting it.

steps.do: Open the child's homework.
steps.expect: The same item — the parent sees what was set, not a summary of it.

name: A fee collected moves three numbers
why: Money is the relation a school checks first. One receipt has to change the family's dues, the day's collection, and the invoice's own state.

steps.do: Collect a part payment against an outstanding invoice and issue the receipt.
steps.expect: A receipt number is issued and the invoice moves to part-paid.

steps.do: Open fees.
steps.expect: Dues have fallen by exactly what was paid, and the receipt is downloadable.

steps.do: Look at today's collection.
steps.expect: “Collected today” includes the payment.

name: Staff leave becomes somebody else's period
why: The chain the timetable turns on: leave approved in the morning has to produce a named cover before the period starts.

steps.do: Apply for one day's leave, with a reason.
steps.expect: It is listed as pending.

steps.do: Approve it.
steps.expect: The teacher is notified, and the row moves to approved.

steps.do: Open the board for that date.
steps.expect: Their periods are listed uncovered, with free staff offered for each.

steps.do: Assign a proxy to one period.
steps.expect: It reads covered; the proxy is notified. Assigning somebody already teaching that period is refused, naming the clash.

name: A student asks for leave and the class teacher answers
why: New. A student could not start this chain at all until today — the feature existed only on the parent's menu.

steps.do: Apply for two days, with a reason.
steps.expect: Listed as waiting on the school. No “Child” column — every row is you.

steps.do: Open student leave requests as that child's class teacher.
steps.expect: The application is there to decide.

steps.do: Approve it.
steps.expect: The student is notified, and the row is approved.

steps.do: Open leave for that child.
steps.expect: The child's own application is visible to the family too.

name: A parent writes and the teacher writes back
why: New. The parent could always send; the teacher had no inbox that surfaced it, so the reply leg could never complete.

steps.do: Write to one of the child's teachers.
steps.expect: The message is sent and shows in your thread.

steps.do: Open Messages and switch to the Parents register.
steps.expect: The thread is listed, named by the parent, with the child underneath and an unread badge. The notification links straight to it.

steps.do: Reply.
steps.expect: The reply sends; the unread badge clears.

steps.do: Reopen the thread.
steps.expect: The teacher's reply is there.

name: Marks become a report card the family reads
why: Four roles touch one number: who may enter it, who may collate it, and who may read it. It is also where the subject-teacher rule is proved.

steps.do: Open marks entry as a subject teacher.
steps.expect: The paper dropdown offers only the subjects you are allocated — not every subject of the class.

steps.do: Enter marks for your subject and save.
steps.expect: Saved. A mark above the paper's maximum is refused.

steps.do: As the class teacher of that section, generate report cards.
steps.expect: Generated for the section. A teacher who is not its class teacher is refused.

steps.do: Open the child's report card.
steps.expect: The mark entered in step 2 is on it.

name: An applicant becomes a student with a bill
why: The longest chain in the product: admissions, students, fees and the parent portal all have to agree about one child.

steps.do: Add a lead, then convert it to an application.
steps.expect: The application appears at the first stage.

steps.do: Take it through to accepted.
steps.expect: Status accepted.

steps.do: Enrol the accepted applicant into a class and section.
steps.expect: A student record and admission number are created — without retyping the child's details.

steps.do: Generate the instalment for that class.
steps.expect: The new child is billed. A class with its own fee structure is billed from that one, not from the all-classes structure.

steps.do: Sign in as that family.
steps.expect: The invoice is waiting.

name: Payroll pays, tells, and cannot be told twice
why: Money leaving the school, plus the notification and email legs — and the state has to survive a page reload.

steps.do: Run the month.
steps.expect: Gross, deductions and net per member of staff. Unmarked staff attendance blocks the run, naming how many.

steps.do: Lock, download the bank file, then mark it paid.
steps.expect: Each step offers only the next one.

steps.do: Publish payslips, then reload the page.
steps.expect: It reads Published — not “Paid” with a Publish button. This is B6.

steps.do: Open My pay.
steps.expect: The payslip for that month, with the breakup, plus a notification and an email.

name: A circular reaches exactly who it named
why: Broadcast is the easiest thing to get silently wrong — it can report twelve recipients and reach nobody.

steps.do: Write a circular to one audience — a class, or all parents.
steps.expect: It reports how many people it will reach.

steps.do: Open its delivery list.
steps.expect: Every named recipient, so “reached 12” can be checked against 12 names.

steps.do: Sign in as somebody in that audience.
steps.expect: The circular is at the top of the bell.

name: The bus a child takes is one fact everywhere
why: Transport is read by the family, the office and the front desk, and each was reading it from a different place.

steps.do: Allot a child to a route with a pick-up and drop stop.
steps.expect: The allocation is saved against that child.

steps.do: Open the child's bus.
steps.expect: The same route and stop.

steps.do: Open that child's record, Transport tab.
steps.expect: Route, vehicle, pick-up and drop with times — not “not built yet”.

name: A visitor at the gate is found, checked and signed out
why: The front desk's whole job, and the one place a wrong name matters at the gate.

steps.do: Sign a visitor in against a host.
steps.expect: The host dropdown lists staff with their employee code — not an empty list. A pass number is issued.

steps.do: Try to sign in somebody on the block list.
steps.expect: Refused, naming the reason.

steps.do: Sign them out.
steps.expect: Minutes on site are recorded; “on the premises” falls by one.

steps.do: Walk to the call log from the menu.
steps.expect: It opens on Calls — not on the visitor form.

name: A certificate is asked for, signed, and downloaded
why: A request that crosses from the family into the office and back out as a file.

steps.do: Request a bonafide certificate.
steps.expect: Listed as requested.

steps.do: Issue it.
steps.expect: A serial number is allotted and the record snapshot is frozen into it.

steps.do: Reopen requests.
steps.expect: It is ready, and downloads.

steps.do: Open that child's Documents tab.
steps.expect: The certificate with its serial and issue date.

name: A library book leaves and comes back
why: The librarian's counter and the student's own shelf are the same loan seen from two sides.

steps.do: Issue a book to a student.
steps.expect: Due date set; copies available falls by one.

steps.do: Open the library.
steps.expect: The loan and its due date.

steps.do: Return it late.
steps.expect: A fine is raised at the school's own rate.

name: A remark written about a child is a remark the family reads
why: The visibility flag is the whole point — a private note must stay private.

steps.do: Write a remark with “Family can see this” on.
steps.expect: Saved, and the family is notified.

steps.do: Open remarks.
steps.expect: The remark is there.

steps.do: Write a second one with that switch off.
steps.expect: It stays on the staff side only — the family must not see it.

name: A promotion closes one year and opens the next
why: The one operation that rewrites a child's history, and the history tab has to show both ends of it.

steps.do: Promote a section into the next class.
steps.expect: It reports how many moved.

steps.do: Open one of those children, History tab.
steps.expect: Two rows: last year marked promoted, this year active — with class, section and roll number.

steps.do: Open the child.
steps.expect: The new class and section.
